description.narrative: New Vision Printing and Publishing Company Limited is Uganda’s leading media group and is the lead partner in this programme alongside Travel care – a travel agency managed by an Irish businessman, and the Ministry of Education and Sports. This innovative partnership brings together partners that share the ambition to support sustainable development and quality education in Uganda involving corporate social responsibility on the part of two private sector entities.The Teachers Making a Difference (TMAD) Program aims to recognise teachers who go beyond the call of duty to use limited resources to deliver quality education- they are nominated by the public before a selection process with a jury. This year’s selection will target and award 12 outstanding teachers including those in vocational education as well as recognise the Most Progressive Alumni (MPA). This is a good example of an innovative public-private partnership with very high levels of visibility for Ireland. Since 2019, the programme has also included linkage with an Irish Teacher training College in Ireland (Mary Immaculate college in Limerick), that provides the professional training to the winning teachers alongside school visits. The programme supports implementation of Uganda’s National Teacher Policy and the Teacher Incentive Framework through recognition and award of outstanding Ugandan teachers as a means of motivation and recognition. In 2022 TMAD winners were awarded as part of the National Teacher Awards by HE the president of Uganda, while 2023 winners were recognised and awarded by the First Lady (Minister of Education and Sports), to which a commitment was made to support the other six teachers alongside the top six travel to Ireland this year. New vision emphasises targeting of teachers handling children with special learning needs for nomination, selection and award particularly use of extra efforts of innovation and creativity. The Teachers Making a Difference (TMD) project is not primarily about gender equality, but about recognizing and building teacher capacity. However, it explicitly integrates gender considerations in the selection process (gender balance required in awardees and travel slots), targeting child mothers for re-enrolment efforts, and focusing on teachers from marginalized areas, which often includes a gender lens. These deliberate actions make gender a meaningful component.
